jobs.title: Manual QA Engineer
jobs.description: We are FundCount , an international fintech company with a 20-year track record of delivering innovative solutions. Our unified software platform powers investment, general, and partnership accounting, providing operational efficiency and insights to family offices, fund administrators, and alternative fund managers worldwide. We’re looking for a Manual QA Engineer to join our growing Quality Assurance team. As part of our team, you’ll play a crucial role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our product. You'll engage in manual testing to uncover bugs and work closely with our development team to ensure flawless releases. We are a fully remote company, and you can work from anywhere except Russia and Belarus. About the Product & Team: Our technology stack includes: Java (Hibernate, Spring, Swing, JUnit4, Mockito) Gradle PostgreSQL, MySQL Git We follow a one-month release cycle, freezing code two weeks before each release. We document our processes in Confluence and manage our tasks in Jira (in English). The development team primarily communicates in Russian via Slack. Our QA team consists of 8 engineers. What you will do: Perform thorough manual testing of desktop and web applications. Write detailed bug reports in Jira. Create and maintain test cases in TestRail. Collaborate with developers and product teams throughout the development lifecycle. What we expect from you: 2+ years of experience in manual testing. Solid understanding of Agile methodologies, SDLC, and CI/CD practices. Intermediate or higher English proficiency (written). Ability to independently research and gather information from documentation and public sources. Adaptability to work with different technologies and tools, with a focus-solving rather than specific experience. Technical Skills: Experience testing both desktop and web (frontend and backend) applications. Proficient in SQL and the ability to write DML queries. Confident in working with Windows/Linux terminals.Experience with version control systems (Git). Ability to read and interpret application logs and troubleshoot stack traces. Familiarity with scripting languages like PowerShell, Bash, or cmd/bat. Would be nice if: Basic programming knowledge in any language. Experience or interest in accounting, finance, or investment (e.g., personal involvement in stock markets). We will be glad to offer you: Fully remote work with a flexible schedule. Corporate benefits. Transparent processes with minimal bureaucracy. If you’re ready to contribute to a fast-growing fintech company and work with a talented team, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today! Originally posted on Himalayas

You’ll help the team understand trends and spot where improvements are needed. Because we’re an early-stage and fully remote company, we’re looking for an individual who can work independently to align the teams involved in building the product. A deep understanding of the technical engineering space (how engineering teams operate, where the friction points typically live, and what good looks like) is essential to being effective and credible in this role. Ability to think on one’s feet, enjoy collaborating with highly technical teams, operate comfortably in ambiguity without a clearly defined deliverable, and be comfortable working asynchronously is essential. Key Responsibilities You will work as part of the TPM team to: Own the processes for bug tracking, incidents, reliability, and escalations, and continuously improve them to drive efficiency and progress toward EPD’s operational health goals. Spot trends across operational health data and translate them into clear insights on how EPD is doing and where improvement is needed. Build dashboards and reports in tools like Jira and Snowflake that give EPD and the broader company visibility into operational health and progress. Turn data into a clear story: what it’s telling us, why it matters, and what needs to change, then design and implement the process changes to act on it. Identify process gaps with EPD and proactively develop just the right amount of process to fill the gap: not too much, not too little. Support planning activities and project tracking processes, helping keep them running smoothly and consistently across EPD. Help run project status reviews, leadership roadmap reviews, and priority reviews, making sure the right information is ready and the right people are in the room. Connect the dots across systems, processes, and teams, spotting where disconnected efforts overlap, conflict, or could be simplified, and acting on it. Jump in on whatever initiative pops up in EPD that needs support, structure, or someone to help carry it forward, whether or not it fits inside a defined program. Handle project retrospectives involving participants and stakeholders to understand what went well and what should be adjusted in future project work. Seek opportunities to bring about ongoing improvement and simplification in business operating procedures and practices, leading to improved efficiency and effectiveness. Each side has its own users and goals, and each shapes the other. Helping both sides succeed together is what makes this role so interesting. You’ll work closely with customers on both sides and with a collaborative team that’s building something new in the creator economy. You’ll bring what you learn back to the Product Director and the team, help shape where the product goes, and then work alongside design and engineering to bring it to life. This is a hands-on role that mixes customer conversations, product definition, and day-to-day delivery. If you enjoy turning what you learn from customers into shipped features, and you like doing it with a team that moves fast and supports each other, we’d love to meet you. About Us Xsolla is a global commerce company with robust tools and services to help developers solve the inherent challenges of the video game industry. From indie to AAA, companies partner with Xsolla to help them fund, distribute, market, and monetize their games. Grounded in the belief in the future of video games, Xsolla is resolute in the mission to bring opportunities together, and continually make new resources available to creators. Headquartered and incorporated in Los Angeles, California, Xsolla operates as the merchant of record and has helped over 1,500+ game developers to reach more players and grow their businesses around the world. With more paths to profits and ways to win, developers have all the things needed to enjoy the game. For more information, visit xsolla.com. Responsibilities: Research and discovery. Get to know both sides of the XPN marketplace: the game publishers running creator campaigns and the creators bringing those campaigns to life. Talk with customers, gather insights, and keep up with trends in the creator economy and gaming. What you learn shapes where the product goes next. Coordinate the roadmap. Work with the Product Director to turn insights into priorities. Bring ideas and recommendations, balance publisher and creator needs, and help build a roadmap the whole team is excited about. Write product requirements. Turn ideas into clear, well-scoped PRDs that give design and engineering what they need to build with confidence. Manage delivery. Organize the work in Jira and keep design, engineering, and QA aligned and moving from kickoff through release. Track what matters. Define and follow the metrics that show how XPN is working for publishers and creators, and use them to guide what we build next. Keep everyone connected. Be the hub for product communication. Share project status, research, and customer insights with the product team. Keep Business Development, Customer Success, and Marketing up to date on what’s shipping and what it means for our partners. Requirements: Product experience. 3+ years in product management or product ownership, shipping software alongside a dedicated engineering team. Customer insight. You enjoy talking with customers and turning those conversations into insights that shape product decisions. You’re comfortable serving more than one type of user and finding solutions that work for everyone involved. Clear writing. You write product requirements that are easy to follow and help the team get aligned quickly. Engineering partnership. jobs.title: Product Manager at Tratta
jobs.description: About Tratta Tratta is the platform that powers credit and collections at scale, and we try to make it enjoyable to work on. Our clients are collection agencies and law firms recovering debt from consumers. Their account data lands in Tratta and is mapped and validated on the way in. They run email and SMS campaigns off it. Consumers land on a payment portal carrying the client's brand, where they can pay, negotiate a plan or sign an agreement electronically without ever speaking to a collector. Payments clear through us by card, ACH or check, and it all feeds back into reporting that shapes the next campaign. Campaigns, data and payments as one closed loop instead of four vendors stitched together. Every week that loop moves millions of dollars in payments, ingests nearly 100 million rows of client data and serves almost 10 million API requests. About the Product Team The product team is small: two PMs, one designer and a distributed engineering team of about ten. You would be our second product hire. There is no product ops layer, no analyst and no one sitting between you and the client, or between you and the code. The role You will own a set of topics end to end. Not "manage a backlog" in the abstract, but pick up messy input from clients and customer success, turn it into something the team can build, get it shipped, and then make sure it actually gets used. Turn requests into work. Client and CS requests arrive as symptoms, not specs. You dig into what is actually being asked, decide whether it is a bug, a gap, a training problem or a real product need, and write it up so a developer can pick it up without a meeting. Prioritize. You decide what gets built next among a lot of competing, legitimate asks, and you can explain the reasoning to a client, a developer and a founder in three different ways. Firefight. Bugs and urgent client issues will land on you. You triage, reproduce, escalate the real ones, and close the loop with whoever raised it. Discovery. You help figure out what we should build next, from client conversations, usage data and your own read of the market. Data. You are comfortable with data end to end: getting it, questioning it, and deciding what to do about it. Own outcomes, not output. Shipping is the midpoint, not the finish line. If a feature launches and nobody knows it exists or nobody adopts it, that is your problem to solve. You will write the client email, record the walkthrough, check the numbers a month later and tell us honestly whether it worked. Wear multiple hats. Small changes you can do yourself with Claude, you do yourself. Otherwise: specs, debugging, data and dashboards, release notes, client emails, whatever the topic needs. There is no one to hand it to. What this role is not It is not a role where you write requirements and hand them to someone else. It is not a role with a defined scope that stays defined. And it is not a role where you can be effective while waiting to be told what to do. How we work Very little process and very few meetings. No planning ritual that exists to justify the previous planning ritual. If something is not working, we change it the next day. The tradeoff is that nothing will be handed to you. There is no queue of pre-groomed tickets, no one checking whether you did the thing, and no process to hide behind if a topic quietly stalls. Autonomy and accountability come as a pair here. We use Claude heavily across product work: analysis, drafting, prototyping, bulk operations across Linear, Slack, HubSpot and our data. Being fluent with AI tooling is not a bonus point, it is how the job gets done at this team size. You will do well here if you Have shipped real product in a small team Are comfortable being close to the technical detail: reading logs, querying data, understanding an API contract, reproducing a bug before you file it Write clearly and briefly Prefer deciding with 70% of the information over waiting for 100% Are direct.
